A small notebook of mechanistic-interpretability experiments on tiny
language models. The recurring move: write down the simplest possible
mathematical model of some LLM behaviour ("the embedding has a log axis",
"the predicted distribution is log-Gaussian", "the LM head reads the
log direction"), then test it with linear probes and activation patching.
The simple models are often wrong in interesting ways — and the wrongness
is what teaches you something about what the model is actually doing.

Everything here reproduces on a laptop CPU. The models I use are GPT-2
small (124M) and the smaller Pythia variants (70M, 160M), chosen so
experiments run in minutes, not hours.

If you want to read the source, the Python scripts that produce every
figure are linked at the bottom of each post.
